authorship.option_contract: Distractor option text is the frozen competitor_concept string verbatim, under the unchanged option realization contract. The 32-of-32 measurement in the option-failure diagnosis showed that layer was already lossless and it is not redesigned here.
authorship.rationale_contract: Every distractor rationale says why the option is plausible, which stem evidence bears on it, and which cited discriminator makes it inferior. The V1 template clause 'That condition is not met here' is not used anywhere: a rationale may only assert a condition unmet where the stem states it contrary, and where the stem is silent the rationale says what outweighs it instead.
authorship.rule: One generation attempt per opportunity, no retry to improve a score. Only the five opportunities whose V2 blueprint is satisfiable are authored; the other five are NO_SAFE_ITEM and no prose exists for them.
authorship.stem_contract: Each stem realizes its blueprint exactly: every PRESENT feature stated, every ABSENT feature stated as absent, and no other feature of the study unit's frozen vocabulary asserted in either direction. Prose that carries no vocabulary feature is free clinical colour.

G2-MED-03.ambiguity_declared: A right-sided electrocardiogram to look at V4R is a reasonable parallel action and a candidate might offer it. It confirms the physiology rather than changing the immediate haemodynamic step, and it is an investigation rather than a management action, so it does not compete with the answer on this lead-in.
G2-MED-03.answer_offered: Give intravenous fluid cautiously to optimise right-sided filling and reassess the response, while the transfer for reperfusion continues.
G2-MED-03.difficulty_comment: Three findings have to be integrated and the reflex responses to two of them, the low pressure and the raised venous pressure, both point the wrong way.
G2-MED-03.reasoning: Inferior ST-elevation with hypotension, a raised jugular venous pressure and clear lungs is right-ventricular infarction physiology. Output is preload dependent, so the immediate move is a careful fluid challenge with reassessment, and preload-reducing treatment and beta blockade are to be avoided while the output is low.

G2-OBGYN-01.ambiguity_declared: DECLARED RISK. CLM-R2-OB-MASTITIS-ANCHOR puts inflammatory mastitis and bacterial mastitis on one spectrum and gives inflammatory mastitis systemic signs such as fever and chills too, separating the two by whether antibiotics are needed to resolve it. That is a response-to-treatment criterion and nothing at presentation settles it, so a candidate who answered inflammatory mastitis would be answering from the same cited packet. CLM-GEN-OB-DX-01 treats this picture as lactational mastitis without drawing the gradation. The two cited packets are at different granularities and the stem cannot resolve the difference.
G2-OBGYN-01.answer_offered: Lactational mastitis with systemic illness, treated as bacterial.
G2-OBGYN-01.difficulty_comment: One salient discriminator per competitor; a recognition item.
G2-OBGYN-01.reasoning: One segment of one breast on day eleven, red, warm and tender, with a fever of 38.6 degrees and rigors. Engorgement is bilateral and early; a plugged duct carries no systemic illness; there is no fluctuance to suggest a collection; the temporary softening after a feed fits milk in the segment rather than a retention cyst, which would not be febrile.

G2-PHELO-01.difficulty_comment: Four results have to be read together, but each competitor is closed by its own stated result, so the reasoning is checklist-like once the pattern is seen.
G2-PHELO-01.reasoning: Survival measured from diagnosis is longer while deaths are unchanged, which is what happens when the diagnosis date moves earlier and the date of death does not. The three usual competitors are each closed by a stated result: randomisation removes self-selection, an equal cumulative number diagnosed removes an excess of detected disease, and an equal grade distribution removes an excess of slowly progressing tumours.

G2-PHELO-02.ambiguity_declared: DECLARED RISK. The stem does not say whether the letter already tells people that attending is a choice. A candidate could read the autonomy objective as calling first for an explicit statement that participation is voluntary, which CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS supports as an autonomy measure in its own right. The stem closes this only by describing the benefit sentence as the thing the rewrite is about, which is an inference rather than a statement.
G2-PHELO-02.answer_offered: Give the reader the absolute chance of benefit, and the chance of a false positive result, instead of the relative figure alone.
G2-PHELO-02.difficulty_comment: Two stated facts, and the work is recognising that a relative figure is not information the reader can act on.
G2-PHELO-02.reasoning: A third fewer deaths is a relative statement that an individual cannot apply to themselves. Where the stated objective is that each person makes their own decision, the letter has to carry figures that describe what happens to a person like the reader, benefit and harm both.

G2-PHELO-03.answer_offered: Do not launch yet; defer until the confirmatory and treatment pathway can carry the numbers.
G2-PHELO-03.difficulty_comment: The shortfall is stated as absolute and unfixable, so once it is read the answer follows with little inference. Declared HARD; this reads EASY.
G2-PHELO-03.reasoning: A screening programme needs somewhere for its positives to go. Labelling asymptomatic people as possibly having a disease that cannot then be investigated or treated is the harm, and no amount of good evaluation planning substitutes for the missing pathway.

distractor_rationales.SEED-G2-MED-T02-BETA-BLOCKER: Plausible: reducing myocardial oxygen demand is a standard early move in an ST-elevation infarct, and his heart rate and pain invite it. Inferior: the stem states hypotension, and CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 says not to initiate or escalate beta blockade during a low-output state or with cardiogenic-shock risk, and to reassess after stabilization. The condition under which this becomes right, a patient out of the low-output state, is the opposite of what the stem describes.
distractor_rationales.SEED-G2-MED-T02-DIURETIC: Plausible: a jugular venous pressure visible at the earlobe reads as volume overload, and a loop diuretic is the reflex response to it. Inferior: the stem states that the lung fields are clear, so there is no pulmonary congestion for a diuretic to relieve, and the raised filling pressure here is the physiology sustaining output rather than a surplus. The same claim directs avoiding preload-reducing diuretics in this pattern.
distractor_rationales.SEED-G2-MED-T02-VASOPRESSOR: Plausible: the blood pressure is 78/50 mmHg and vasoactive support is part of managing infarct-related shock. Inferior: preload has not yet been optimized, and CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 puts a cautious fluid challenge with reassessment first in exactly this pattern. CLM-ACS-AMI-CARDIOGENIC-SHOCK-01 reserves vasoactive support for persistent hypotension or a vasopressor requirement with end-organ hypoperfusion, which is the point at which this option becomes the right one.

G2-MED-03.key_option_text: Give a cautious intravenous fluid bolus and reassess fluid responsiveness
G2-MED-03.key_rationale: Hypotension with a raised jugular venous pressure and clear lung fields in an inferior ST-elevation infarct identifies right-ventricular infarction physiology, in which cardiac output depends on right-sided filling. CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 directs cautious preload optimization with intravenous fluid and reassessment of fluid responsiveness for the hypotension, alongside the reperfusion that is already being arranged.
G2-MED-03.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?
G2-MED-03.stem: A 64-year-old man arrives at a community emergency department 70 minutes after the sudden onset of heavy central chest pain. His electrocardiogram shows 3 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal depression in I and aVL. The regional percutaneous coronary intervention centre has accepted him and the transfer arranged will place him on the catheterisation laboratory table well inside the accepted first-medical-contact-to-device interval. While the transfer is being organised his blood pressure falls to 78/50 mmHg. His jugular venous pressure is visible at the earlobe with the head of the bed at 45 degrees, and his lung fields are clear throughout.

distractor_rationales.SEED-OB-T01-ABSCESS: Plausible: an abscess is a progression of this same infection and shares its systemic features, so nothing in the fever or the erythema separates the two. Inferior: CLM-R2-OB-ABSCESS describes progressive induration and erythema with often a palpable fluid collection in a well-defined area, and CLM-GEN-OB-INV-01 makes fluctuance the finding that raises the concern. The stem states that no fluctuant area and no pocket of fluid can be felt, which is the condition under which this would be the answer.
distractor_rationales.SEED-OB-T01-GALACTOCELE: Plausible: the swelling decreases temporarily after a feed, which is exactly the behaviour CLM-R4-OB-GALACTOCELE describes for a galactocele. Inferior: the same claim says a galactocele does not carry erythema or systemic symptoms unless it becomes infected, and the stem states both a red, warm segment and a fever with rigors.
distractor_rationales.SEED-OB-T01-IBC: Plausible: a red, swollen breast in a young woman is the presentation that must not be assumed benign, and CLM-R2-OB-IBC makes any concern for it an urgent referral. Inferior: that claim raises the concern on skin thickening, breast retraction and a peau d'orange appearance, none of which is described here, while the acute fever and rigors of the last day belong to the infective picture rather than to a neoplastic one.

G2-OBGYN-01.key_rationale: CLM-R2-OB-MASTITIS-ANCHOR describes an increasingly erythematous, oedematous and painful region of the breast with systemic signs such as fever and chills, and CLM-GEN-OB-DX-01 adds unilateral localized tenderness, erythema and heat with fever or malaise. One segment of one breast is involved on day eleven with a fever of 38.6 degrees, which is that pattern.
G2-OBGYN-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?
G2-OBGYN-01.stem: A 29-year-old woman is seen on the eleventh day after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is breastfeeding and describes two days of increasing pain in the upper outer part of her right breast. That segment is red, swollen, warm and tender, and the swelling becomes noticeably smaller for a while after her baby has fed from that side. Her temperature is 38.6 degrees Celsius and she has felt shivery and generally unwell since yesterday. No fluctuant area and no pocket of fluid can be felt anywhere in the breast.

the swelling becomes noticeably smaller for a while after her baby has fed from that side

distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T01-HEALTHY-SCREENEE: Plausible: better outcomes in a screened group are very often explained by who chooses to be screened, and CLM-R2-PHELO-HEALTHY-VOLUNTEER says such comparisons tend to favour the screened. Inferior: that mechanism needs groups that selected themselves, and the stem states that participants were randomly assigned and comparable at entry, which is the condition under which this explanation would apply.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T01-LENGTH: Plausible: intermittent screening does preferentially catch slowly progressing disease, and CLM-R2-PHELO-LENGTH explains why that inflates survival. Inferior: that mechanism requires an excess of slow-progressing variants among screen-detected cases, and the stem states that the distribution of tumour grade was the same in both groups.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T01-OVERDIAGNOSIS: Plausible: overdiagnosis also produces longer measured survival with unchanged mortality, so the two headline results alone do not separate it from the answer. Inferior: CLM-R2-PHELO-OVERDIAGNOSIS identifies it by an excess of cancers diagnosed in the screened group, and the stem states that the cumulative number diagnosed was the same in the two groups.

G2-PHELO-01.key_rationale: CLM-R2-PHELO-LEAD-TIME describes the delay between the point at which disease becomes detectable by screening and the point at which it would have been diagnosed from symptoms, and warns that judging a programme by survival time after diagnosis gives a falsely positive impression. Every element of that is here: the diagnosis date moves earlier, the survival clock therefore starts earlier, and the date of death does not move, which is why mortality is unchanged while measured survival is four years longer.
G2-PHELO-01.lead_in: Which explanation best accounts for this pattern of results?
G2-PHELO-01.stem: A national trial randomly assigned 80,000 adults either to a new screening test for a solid tumour or to usual care, and the two groups were comparable at entry. After twelve years of follow-up the cumulative number of cancers diagnosed was the same in the two groups, and the distribution of tumour grade among the cancers found was also the same in the two groups. Deaths from the cancer did not differ between the groups. Among people whose cancer was found by screening, however, the average time from diagnosis to death was four years longer than among those diagnosed in usual care.

distractor_rationales.SEED-G2-PHELO-T02-VOLUNTARY: Plausible: a voluntariness statement is itself an autonomy measure, and CLM-R2-PHELO-REMINDERS warns that people who read more authority into an invitation than it has may abdicate their right to informed consent. Inferior: that is the repair for a letter whose defect is that readers feel obliged to attend, and the defect the stem describes is a different one, that the only benefit figure given cannot be applied to the reader.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T02-DETECTION-COUNT: Plausible: it replaces a relative figure with a real count, which looks like the concrete information the letter is missing. Inferior: a detection count without the number invited and without the harms is another figure the reader cannot apply to themselves, and the stem states that the letter carries no denominator and no account of harm. Its condition, that the reader already has both, is not met.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T02-SENSITIVITY: Plausible: sensitivity and specificity are the standard description of a screening test's performance and belong in programme documentation, per CLM-R4-PHELO-ACTION-POLICY. Inferior: they describe the test rather than the reader's own chance of benefit or harm, and CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY makes protecting autonomy a matter of how the information lands with the person invited, which is the objective the stem states.

G2-PHELO-02.key_option_text: Give the absolute chance of benefit and of a false positive result
G2-PHELO-02.key_rationale: CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE contrasts a relative statement, which sounds impressive, with an absolute figure, which is what actually helps an individual decide, and CLM-R4-PHELO-FALSEPOS supplies the corresponding harm that a first-time attender faces. CLM-R2-PHELO-ACCEPTABILITY says autonomy may be compromised by the way information is given, so where informed choice is the stated objective the figures given have to be ones the reader can apply to themselves.
G2-PHELO-02.lead_in: Which revision to the letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?
G2-PHELO-02.stem: A regional screening programme is rewriting the letter it sends to the people it invites for a first screening test. The programme board has agreed that the purpose of the rewrite is to protect the autonomy of those invited, so that each of them can make their own decision about whether to attend. The current letter describes the benefit in one sentence: that screening reduces deaths from the disease by about a third. It says nothing else about how much benefit an individual can expect.

distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T03-EVALUATE: Plausible: continuing evaluation against defined goals is a genuine requirement, CLM-R4-PHELO-EVALUATION states it, and this programme already has the goals and the plan the stem describes. Inferior: it is a requirement of a programme that does launch, and the stem states the confirmatory pathway cannot take the expected numbers. Evaluating a programme as it produces positives it cannot investigate does not prevent that harm.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T03-PILOT: Plausible: reducing scale is the usual way to launch within a constraint, and CLM-R2-PHELO-COST-CONTINUITY notes that population-scale cost is what makes screening hard to sustain. Inferior: a pilot works where the constraint is cost or logistics, and the stem describes an absolute shortfall in the confirmatory pathway with no additional capacity available at all, so a single district reproduces the same failure on a smaller scale.
distractor_rationales.SEED-PHELO-T03-RAISE-CUTOFF: Plausible: raising the threshold does reduce the number of positive results and therefore the referral load, and CLM-R2-PHELO-CUTOFF treats the placement of the cut-off as a real design decision. Inferior: that claim makes a cut-off set too far toward the low-risk end a matter of investigating and reassuring large numbers of low-risk people, and the stem does not describe that. Moving the threshold does not create a confirmatory pathway, and the people who still screen positive meet the same shortfall.

G2-PHELO-03.key_option_text: Defer the launch until diagnostic and treatment capacity is in place
G2-PHELO-03.key_rationale: CLM-GEN-PHELO-ORG-01 makes coordinated capacity for confirmatory diagnosis and treatment a requirement of a screening programme and says a test should not be launched at population scale when that pathway cannot be delivered. CLM-R4-PHELO-HARM-LABEL names the harm precisely: labelling asymptomatic people as possibly having a disease when the investigation cannot follow, or diagnosing them with no treatment to offer. CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES reaches the same conclusion where follow-up is not accessible.
G2-PHELO-03.lead_in: What should the programme do about the planned launch?
G2-PHELO-03.stem: A provincial health authority has finished planning a population screening programme for a chronic condition. The programme has written goals, a defined target population and an evaluation plan that will report against those goals each year. During final preparations the authority establishes that the specialist clinics that would confirm the diagnosis in people who screen positive, and the services that would treat them, cannot take the numbers the programme expects, and that no additional confirmatory or treatment capacity can be secured for the foreseeable future.
